parity: make test PARITY OK 675/675; make test-stages PARITY OK 620/620 (615 + this feature's 5); make check-spec OK; kuna catalog --check OK; tests/cli 28/28
filed_hypothesis: ADVISORY. The undiscovered callback has no prototype evidence, and parameter recovery fails to promote live-in R8D/R9D values to arguments.
speed_method: interleaved min/median of 15 alternating runs of the witness (kuna decompile lugosiii 0x6500 --addr), plus interleaved min-of-3 whole-binary decompile-all on three binaries
decisions: THE FILED HYPOTHESIS IS OVERTURNED, though the symptom stands exactly as filed. 'No prototype evidence, so live-in R8D/R9D are not promoted' is not what happens. ActionInputPrototype registers a trial for every input Varnode and marks it ACTIVE when it has descendants, so rdi, r8d AND r9d all reach ParamListStandard::fillinMap as active trials with no prototype anywhere -- and buildTrialMap even synthesizes unreferenced filler trials for the ignored rsi/rdx/rcx. Prototype evidence is not the discriminating variable.

THE DISCRIMINATING VARIABLE IS THE WIDTH OF THE REGISTER HOLE, isolated in a 30-line fixture built for the purpose. Two callbacks, both reachable only through a function-pointer table, both without a prototype: on_two (rdi and rcx read, rsi/rdx dead -- a TWO-register hole) recovers `void on_two(long a0,unsigned long a1,unsigned long a2,int a3)` on unmodified main, filler parameters and all; on_key (rdi, r8d, r9d read, rsi/rdx/rcx dead -- a THREE-register hole) renders `void on_key(long a0)` with `int v1; // r8d` and `int v2; // r9d` read out of nowhere. The difference is one slot of gap.

ROOT CAUSE: ParamListStandard::forceInactiveChain (fspec.cc:1519) is called with maxchain = 2. It counts consecutive unused parameter slots and, once the run passes two, sets seenchain and marks EVERY remaining trial inactive -- including trials that already scored active. fillinMap then only marks the still-active trials used. The witness's hole is exactly three registers, one past the limit.

WHY THE RULE IS RIGHT WHERE IT CAME FROM AND WRONG HERE. forceInactiveChain is shared between call-site argument recovery and the function's own input recovery. At a call site a trial is scored ACTIVE from the CALLER's data flow (checkInputTrialUse: an argument register holding a value the caller wrote and does not otherwise use), which is genuinely ambiguous, so a long run of empty slots really is evidence the recovery walked past the end of the list -- calleedeadarg's record names the same rule from the other side. For the function's own inputs an ACTIVE trial is a fact about the body: it reads that caller-saved register before any definition of it. The gap slots carry no counter-evidence at all, since an untouched argument register is exactly what an ignored parameter looks like -- and a callback whose signature is fixed by the API it is registered with ignores parameters as a matter of course.

THE FIRST DESIGN WAS WRONG AND THE CORPUS SWEEP CAUGHT IT, which is the single most important thing in this record. Draft 1 suppressed seenchain for any register GAP SLOT. It fixed the witness and passed 675/675, and it also let one Win64 sub_140010a57 (CrackVM-V2.exe) span its four-register hole and keep walking into the stack resource, promoting eleven scratch slots of the caller's argument area into a FIFTEEN-parameter signature with `a4 = 0; a5 = 0;` assignments to parameters. Sweep totals for draft 1: 343 changed functions, 12 of them with more than 20 residual diff lines.

DRAFT 2 (reset the chain at a register gap slot instead of suppressing the veto) DID NOT FIX IT, measured rather than assumed: sub_140010a57's stack trials are contiguous, so there was no second run for the reset to catch. Recorded because the reasoning is plausible and someone will try it again.

SHIPPED RULE: an ACTIVE trial whose own ParamEntry is an EXCLUSION (register) entry is never demoted by forceInactiveChain during the function's own input recovery. A stack trial's fate is left exactly to upstream. The evidence this option rests on -- read-before-written -- is a register's: a caller-saved argument register read live-in can only carry a value the caller placed there, while a positive-offset stack slot read live-in is much weaker (the Win64 home area is routinely scratch, and an over-wide or aliased read looks identical). Because trials sort into formal parameter order, protecting only register trials also keeps the existing hole-filling tail loop inside the register file, so the gain is bounded by the ABI.

PRICE OF THAT NARROWING, PAID KNOWINGLY: a genuine Win64 fifth argument sitting on the stack behind a four-register hole (vm_obfuscation.exe sub_14000c384) reverts to upstream's `void sub_14000c384(void)`. Draft 1 recovered it. It is not what this need is about and it is not separable from the fifteen-parameter failure by any local property measured here, so the conservative arm was taken.

SWEEP, RUN TWICE (once per draft) OVER 83 REAL-WORLD BINARIES, 36,589 DECOMPILED FUNCTIONS. Shipped rule: 196 functions changed (0.54%). Every single one is additive -- parameter-count gain of +4 (149), +5 (45) or +6 (2), never a loss and never a same-arity change. Every declaration dropped from a changed function's block is a REGISTER (r8, r9, r9d, r8d, ecx, rcx, ...); zero stack declarations were dropped, which is the shipped narrowing holding empirically. 0 of 196 had ANY statement-list difference after normalizing vN/aN identifiers: the pass adds register parameters and renames the undefined locals they replace, and moves, deletes and re-anchors nothing. Function sets were identical between arms on every binary; the 9 binaries that failed to load failed under BOTH arms.

SPEED: scripts.pipeline.timeit reported -30.52% over 11 samples, twice. That is the known sequential-measurement artifact (docs/features/returncopysplit measured a -20.23% noise floor on byte-identical output). Interleaved min-of-15 on the same witness reports +0.07% min / +0.33% median, and interleaved min-of-3 whole-binary decompile-all reports +0.27% (vm_obfuscation.exe, 6.1s) and +0.41% (crackme.x86_64.elf, 75.6s). The honest answer is no measurable cost, not a speedup.

IN-REPO COVER, since binary_source is 'dataset' and verify --promote refuses it (the #377/#392/#404 wall). Copied #395's precedent: a new fixture decompiler/crates/kuna-analysis/tests/fixtures/inputparamgap_x86_64 carrying BOTH arms -- on_key (three-register hole, the bug) and on_two (two-register hole, the control that is identical under both settings) -- with tests/cli/keyboard-callback-uses-undefined.json pinned to it and tests/stages/kuna-inputparamgap.xml pinning the two-pass rendering of both.
residue: A stack argument behind a register hole (the Win64 fifth-argument shape) is still dropped, by design. Recovering it needs evidence this option does not have -- something that separates a real stack parameter from the home area used as scratch.
